High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:217940
Court No. - 75
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 46880 of 2023

Applicant :- Vijendra @ Jitendra Yadav
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Jitendra Kumar Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Umesh Chandra Sharma,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The instant bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to enlarge the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 192 of 2023 under Sections 411, 414, 420, 307 I.P.C., Police Station- Shikohabad, District- Firozabad, during the pendency of the trial.
3. Counsel for the applicant contends that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.
The applicant is neither named in the F.I.R. nor arrested from the spot.

His name surfaced in the confessional statement of the co-accused Gaurav, thereafter, the applicant was summoned on warrant-B by the court and on his pointing out a country made pistol has been alleged to be recovered, however, there is no independent witness of the same.
It is contended that in the alleged incident none of police personnel received injuries.
It is next contended that the co-accused Gaurav who has been alleged to be arrested on spot has been granted bail by the Sessions Court itself.
The Vijendra @ Jitendra Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7248953/

entities.text: Vijendra @ Jitendra Yadav vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 criminal history of the applicant has been explained in para 18 of the affidavit.
The applicant is in jail since 15.4.2023, in case he is enlarged on bail, he will not misuse the said liberty.
4. Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for bail but could not satisfactorily dispute the aforesaid submissions from the record.

5. Having regard to the submissions made above and the fact that the applicant has remained confined for seven months, and the co-accused has been enlarged on bail, more so when no reasonable apprehension has been brought to the fore by the State that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, would either temper with the evidence or delay the trial or intimidate the witness, without commenting on the merits of the case, I am of the opinion that the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to move bail cancellation application before this Court.

Order Date :- 16.11.2023 S.Verma  Vijendra @ Jitendra Yadav vs State Of U.P. on 16 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7248953/
